summary.title: Front-end Developer Handbook 2019
summary.one_liner: A yearly curated guide to what front-end development is, how to learn it, which core web technologies and tools matter, and the trends shaping the field in 2019.
keywords: how to become a front-end developer
core web technologies dom http url json
takeaways: Front-end development means producing HTML, CSS and JavaScript that users see and interact with, and it must work across browsers, operating systems and devices.
Learn the underlying technologies (HTML, CSS, DOM, JavaScript) before abstractions such as jQuery, Sass, JSX, TypeScript or Bootstrap.
Front-end job titles differ in meaning; the term 'front-end developer' is ambiguous, with a growing divide between HTML/CSS developers and JavaScript application engineers.
The handbook surveys 2018 trends such as CSS Grid and Flexbox, CSS variables, ES modules, Cypress, Parcel, Babel 7, GraphQL and the rise of jQuery replacement with native DOM.
summary.summary: This is the 2019 edition of an annual handbook by Cody Lindley, sponsored by Frontend Masters, aimed at developers and also managers and recruiters. It opens with a recap of 2018 front-end trends, then defines front-end development and the web runtimes it targets (browsers, headless browsers, webviews, and native-from-web environments). It proposes a learning path that starts with the web platform and core technologies, and explains common front-end job titles. The later sections define core specifications (HTML, CSS, HTTP, URL, JavaScript, JSON, DOM, Web APIs, WCAG/ARIA) with links to their documentation; the listing and page text end before the tools and information-outlet chapters.
